articles.title: Middleton's Regeneration Efforts Accelerate with New Developments
articles.excerpt: Middleton's regeneration initiative has gained momentum with three significant announcements, including plans for the historic Middleton Old Grammar School and the repurposing of the Scout Hut for community use.
articles.content_html:
Middleton's regeneration initiative has received a significant boost with three key announcements made during an event at Middleton Arena on 16 September 2026. The event, which attracted over 500 residents and local business leaders, aimed to update the community on the progress of the Mayoral Development Corporation and the results of the engagement exercise titled 'Our Town, Our Future'.

One of the major developments includes the recent acquisition of the historic Middleton Old Grammar School by Rochdale Borough Council. Founded in 1582, the school was originally established to provide free education to local children. After serving as a wedding and events venue, the council seized the opportunity to purchase the building when it became available. A feasibility study is currently underway to assess the potential for repairing, refurbishing, and reopening the site for community use, with an announcement regarding a new tenant expected before the end of the year.

In addition, the council is in the process of acquiring the long-derelict Warwick Mill and the adjacent London House, a 1960s office block. The aim is to restore Warwick Mill for residential use while demolishing London House. This initiative is part of a broader strategy to revitalise the area and enhance local housing options.

Furthermore, the Middleton Scout Hut, which has been vacant for 13 years, will be transformed into a community venue. The council has agreed to a long-term lease with the Groundwork Trust, a charitable organisation. Plans for the Scout Hut include creating a hub for workshops focused on ecology and construction skills, as well as providing a space for local environmental projects and activities aimed at young people. This development is expected to foster community engagement and help address social isolation.
